subject: Starter Spark — sweetener stacking request & conversion ops split
messages:
From: Harper Lin <harper@founderspark.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Starter Spark — request to stack launch sweeteners

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team loved the latency numbers. We are finalizing our accelerator package and I wanted to check one operational detail before we sign: can Redwood stack the Starter Spark free-credit sweetener (90 days, $5k) with an early-conversion discount that applies if we convert to Dedicated within 9 months?

Concretely FoundersSpark is asking for:
- Keep the existing 90-day $5k credit for cohort participants
- Allow program teams to apply a one-time 15% conversion credit toward Dedicated if they convert their pilot within 9 months
- Permit a single participant to use both — i.e., credits + conversion credit (we want to avoid surprises)

We have a projected pilot of 20 teams; attached is a rough usage projection and a spreadsheet showing cohort timing. Curious what the operational constraints are (billing flow, credit stacking rules, and whether credits can be escrowed to convert).

Also looping my partnerships contact in case you need contract language.

Appreciate quick clarity — our board wants the partner terms locked this week.

Best,
Harper
Partnerships, FoundersSpark

Attachments: FoundersSpark_Sweetener_Request.xlsx (spreadsheet), usage-projection-FoundersSpark.csv (csv)
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Harper Lin <harper@founderspark.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 16:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Starter Spark — request to stack launch sweeteners

Hi Harper — great to hear the demo resonated. Short answer: we can do a stacking path but it requires a small carveout and an ops playbook so accounting can track credits vs. conversion discounts.

High-level options we can offer (pick one):
1) Credits then conversion credit: apply cohort $5k credit first (applies to hosted usage), and a 15% one-time invoice credit if customer signs Dedicated within 9 months. Accounting treats conversion credit as a separate deduction tied to the Dedicated contract.
2) Escrow-to-convert: we place the $5k in an escrow-like hold; if customer converts within 9 months, the hold automatically converts to the 15% applied against committed Dedicated spend (requires a short amendment & finance sign-off).
3) No stacking: credits are mutually exclusive with promotional Dedicated discounts (easiest operationally).

We generally prefer option 1 for speed — low ops friction and predictable recognition. Option 2 is doable but requires a short SOW amendment and Legal/Finance approval.

Ben — can you run a quick P&L impact for option 1 vs option 2 for a 20-team cohort (sheet attached)?
Lauren — FYI on potential accounting treatment and whether we can approve option 2 with a short amendment template.
Marissa — heads-up for CS onboarding expectations if credits convert.

Harper — I’ll aim to turn around a suggested contract paragraph by EOD tomorrow once Ben and Lauren weigh in.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Starter Spark — request to stack launch sweeteners

Quick numbers from my side (assumes cohort average pilot consumes $2,000 of hosted usage in 90 days):
- 20 teams x $2,000 = $40k hosted usage baseline
- Starter Spark credit total: 20 x $5k = $100k face value (we cap per-team redemption to credit available; many teams won't use full $5k)

Option 1 (credits then 15% conversion credit):
- Immediate cost hit: we absorb revenue deferral for credit usage; likely ~35-45% redemption rate based on similar cohorts --> expect $35k - $45k realized usage offset in quarter 1.
- Conversion credit only applies at Dedicated contract signing; if 10% convert in 9 months (2 teams), 15% discount on their committed spend is incremental revenue reduction; manageable at scale.

Option 2 (escrow-to-convert):
- Operational overhead: finance must tie escrow balance to account and reverse entries at conversion; legal amendment needed. Reduced near-term revenue recognition but cleaner conversion math.

Recommendation: approve Option 1 with a cap clause: cohort-level cap of $110k total promotional exposure (credits + future conversion credits) and a 9-month conversion window. This keeps our worst-case contingent liability bounded.

Lauren — please confirm if the $110k cap is good or if Finance wants a tighter threshold.

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:21:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Starter Spark — request to stack launch sweeteners

Thanks Ben + Olga — finance is comfortable with Option 1 with the following controls:
- Binding cohort-level promo exposure cap at $100k (not $110k).
- Require FoundersSpark to sign our two-paragraph promo addendum that:
   * Explicitly states credits apply to hosted usage only and are non-transferable,
   * Defines conversion credit calculation (15% of first 12 months committed Dedicated invoice, capped at $25k per converting team),
   * Requires customer to execute Dedicated contract within 9 months and reference Deal ID FS-2026-089.
- We also want a clause that unused credits expire at 90 days and are not refundable.

If FoundersSpark accepts the addendum language, Legal will pre-sign and we can add the paragraph to the MSA.

Lauren Bishop
Finance Business Partner, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Harper Lin <harper@founderspark.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Starter Spark — request to stack launch sweeteners

Harper — good news: we can do a stacked path and Finance wants a cohort promo cap. Summary of the approved approach (Option 1, with controls):
- Starter Spark cohort credit remains: 90 days, $5k per eligible team; credits apply to hosted usage only and expire at 90 days.
- Conversion credit: one-time 15% credit applied against first 12 months of committed Dedicated invoice; per-team conversion credit capped at $25k.
- Cohort-level promo exposure cap: $100k total for credits + conversion credits.
- Conversion window: 9 months from cohort start; customer must execute Dedicated contract referencing Deal ID FS-2026-089.
- Legal will provide a 2-paragraph promo addendum we can attach to the partnership agreement; Marissa, please prepare a short CS onboarding note for converted teams.

If that works for FoundersSpark, we’ll send the addendum and a short ops runbook documenting billing flags and the escrow/credit accounting flows.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call to finalize wording if helpful.

Olga
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: FoundersSpark_Sweetener_Request.xlsx (accepted_vars tab), usage-projection-FoundersSpark.csv (noted)
